lock_files.notes: Same flock(2) lease files as any-core.sh, both-cores.sh and pf-launch. Lock order: GPU files first (testing-gpu.lock, then testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock), then core leases. Owner job units take them for their lifetime (GPU files handed over by the queue's GPU claim when the GPU was contended); the worker itself only observes /proc/locks. Borrow jobs hold borrow-core<K>.lock shared instead, never the core lease; holding borrow-core<K>.lock exclusively from outside the queue marks core K as not lendable. 16 cores: core K's lease is testing-core<K>.lock for K = 0-5 and 7-15 (core 6: testing-core.lock), its borrow lease borrow-core<K>.lock.

borrow.notes: Borrow jobs (simq submit --borrow) run in simqborrow.slice, a top-level slice of the user manager with cpu.idle=1, as units with CPUWeight=1, SCHED_IDLE and idle I/O class: every owner job unit and every process of the terminal sessions wins the CPU. A lease holder or owner job is idle when its process tree used at most idle_threshold cores above a whole number over idle_window_s and the core itself was at most cpu_idle_threshold busy; a borrower lent such a core is preempted when the tree uses more than the cores left to it plus busy_threshold over busy_window_s. A frozen borrower is requeued after freeze_max_s or shortly before its time limit. backfill_waiting_owners (0.6.3): a free core that a waiting owner job needs is lent only to a borrow job whose time limit ends before that owner job can start (EASY backfill); without it such cores are not lent at all while the owner job waits, which in a single pool would hold every borrow job back whenever any owner job waits.

partitions.name: zenobia
partitions.description: zenobia: one pool of every physical core (from sysfs) and the GPU

notes: The partition names used before 0.6.3 (spheral, raikou-mfem, powerflow) are aliases of zenobia: -p spheral|raikou-mfem|powerflow keeps working, with the defaults those partitions had (cores, memory, time) and their old cores tried first (prefer_cpus); limits are the pool's. A job keeps the name it was submitted with (SIMQ_PARTITION, simq listings). Jobs recorded under these names before 0.6.3 are adopted and scheduled under zenobia.

Without -p a job goes to zenobia with 4 cores, 4G (lowered from the old spheral default 18G on 2026-11-05), 2 days, lowest free cores first. Limits: 20G memory, 14 days (the largest of the old partitions).
memory_schedulable is the sum of --mem over concurrent jobs (31 GiB RAM; about 3 GiB left for the system).
The GPU is a scheduled resource of the pool: exclusive per job unless --gpu-mem is given and the 11G budget allows sharing; queued GPU jobs win the GPU lease files through the GPU line.

Lending: free cores and the idle cores of running owner jobs go to borrow jobs (lend: true). Cores leased by tools outside the queue (any-core.sh, both-cores.sh, pf-launch) are not lent (lend_leased_idle: false). Timing-sensitive runs submit with --exclusive-timing, which keeps the job's cores and their SMT siblings unlent while it runs.
No GPU is ever lent: borrow jobs cannot request GPUs.

0.7.0: the worker is event-driven (woken by submissions, cancellations and job ends through <state>/worker.wake; passes every poll_seconds only while something must be watched, else at most every idle_seconds); job memory is tracked from the units' cgroups (memory section); --mem auto; job state can be reported to GitHub (github section).

0.8.0: cpus "auto": every physical core of the machine read from sysfs (lowest logical CPU of each SMT pair), siblings and L3 domains likewise, so this file serves the 8-core 9850X3D and the 16-core 9950X3D2 alike. Owner jobs get whole physical cores; SMT siblings are never allocated to them. borrow.lend_siblings is false here: a busy process on a sibling slowed an integer-heavy owner on its core by 47% (SHA-NI work by 0.1%) on 2026-11-06, and idle CPU priority cannot help with that (the two threads share the core's execution units). Set it true to lend the siblings to borrow jobs (an owner then keeps its siblings only with --exclusive-timing).

memory_schedulable stays 28G; max_mem 20G. A priority_max_mem (for example {"min_priority": 10, "max_mem": "26G"}) would let priority-10 owner jobs ask for more; it is not set until full-machine pilot memory is measured.

gpu_line.notes: 0.6.2 GPU line. Queued GPU jobs that are ready except for the GPU join the line through a claim unit (<prefix>-gpuclaim-<token>.service) that waits for testing-gpu.lock in the kernel queue, then takes testing-gpu-<UUID>.lock, and hands both open files to the job unit (SCM_RIGHTS), so the lock is never released in between and the job's time limit starts with its unit. gpu-lease users publish tickets in ticket_dir; members are served by since-time (a claim's is the submit time of its oldest ready job, a helper's its start time). Processes blocked in a raw flock on the GPU files (command in requeue_commands, not a job-control job of an interactive shell) are moved behind the line with SIGSTOP+SIGCONT; every move is logged in log_path. state_path lists the waiting queue jobs with their since-times, the claim, the holders and the raw waiters (heartbeat every 10 s; stale after stale_after_s, withdrawn when the worker stops). A held claim that no job takes within claim_hold_max_s releases the GPU.

memory.notes: 0.7.0. Every sample_seconds the worker reads each running job unit's cgroup (memory.current, memory.peak) and /proc/meminfo, with no process spawned; min/max per minute are written to the database every record_seconds; at a job's end its unit records memory.peak and CPU time. Admission guard: a start needs its request <= MemAvailable - margin (null: the high-water mark) - the unallocated requests of jobs started less than ramp_seconds ago; reservations (memory_schedulable) stay the primary limit and are never exceeded on the basis of current use. Memory pressure: MemAvailable below max(high_water_available, high_water_percent of MemTotal) stops dispatch and preempts borrow jobs by their --on-preempt policy (a frozen one is requeued after pressure_escalate_seconds); the jobs that grew are recorded; owner jobs are never stopped for it (their own MemoryMax bounds them); dispatch resumes at max(low_water_available, low_water_percent). --mem auto: auto_factor x the largest of the last auto_history recorded peaks of jobs with the same name (else name family, preferring the same core count), rounded up to auto_round, within the partition's min_mem..max_mem; without history the default. Submit warns when --mem is at least warn_factor x that peak and warn_min_excess above it. 0.7.1: auto_default -- a job submitted without --mem gets --mem auto when its name (or family) has a recorded peak, else the default (4G); the spheral alias's default memory is auto (it was 18G). An explicit --mem always wins.

github.notes: 0.7.0. Jobs submitted with --github-status OWNER/REPO@SHA:CONTEXT get commit statuses from the worker on every transition (pending queued/running, success/failure from the exit code, error for cancel, time limit, OOM kill, preemption-cancel, lost unit); --github-comment OWNER/REPO#PR adds one PR comment at the end, edited in place (marker <!-- simq-job:N -->). Statuses never notify; only the first creation of a comment can. Job text is sanitized (no @mentions, no #N references). One posting thread in the worker; failures retried with backoff; scheduling never waits for GitHub. Token: token_file, else `gh auth token` at post time; kept in memory only.

topology.notes: 0.8.0: L3 domains are read from sysfs at start (cache/index3/shared_cpu_list): one on the 9850X3D, two 8-core domains on the 9950X3D2. A job stays inside one domain when it fits; jobs of at least heavy_cores cores (null: half a domain) go to the least-loaded domain; --l3-domains N / --split-domains A,B ask for several.

containment.notes: 0.7.2. Every job started by 0.7.2 gets its own temporary and MPI rendezvous directory <tmp_base>/simq.<job>.<token12> (mode 700, made by the job wrapper, removed at the job's end): TMPDIR, PMIX_SYSTEM_TMPDIR, PMIX_SERVER_TMPDIR and PRTE_MCA_prte_tmpdir_base point at it (a -e value wins), so Open MPI 5's prun and prterun --dvm search/system cannot find a PRRTE DVM outside the job (they fail instead of spawning the ranks in the DVM's cgroup). Inherited launcher identity variables (PMIX_* but PMIX_MCA_*, PRTE_* but PRTE_MCA_*, PMI_*, OMPI_COMM_WORLD_*, ...) are dropped. Every scan_seconds while job units run, and at each job's end, the worker reads /proc: processes carrying a job's SIMQ_LAUNCH_TOKEN outside its cgroup go to the job's escaped.json, simq show and the worker log; MPI launcher daemons outside every job go to containment.json, simq partitions and simq doctor. Report only: nothing is killed.

scheduler.notes: 0.8.1: the first 8 blocked owner jobs in dispatch order hold backfill reservations, each placed after the ones ahead of it in a resource-time profile; a later job starts now only if every reserved job ahead of it can still start at its reserved time. 1 restores the EASY backfill of 0.8.0 (only the head is protected), under which 30 one-core probes (priority 0, 2 h) took every freed core while five 4-core priority-5 jobs waited 1.5 h behind a 16-core head reserved 8.5 h ahead (2026-11-06). Parked jobs hold no reservation.
